title: Adaptive Quarter Plan: Cohort-based Hosted Endpoint Phasing & Model Retirement
creator: Ava Chen
description: Quarterly plan to phase new hosted endpoint offerings by customer cohort, schedule model retirement windows for older variants, and define canary/rollback policies. Focus is on minimizing customer churn during lineup rotations while preserving capacity headroom and meeting latency SLOs. Plan spans product decisions, capacity allocations, canary cadence, and observability signals for automated rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort definitions (free, starter, enterprise) finalized and approved by PM and Sales
Phased calendar published with canary windows, cutoff dates, and communication milestones
Runbook for model retirement and emergency rollback reviewed by SRE and approved
Capacity hedges (burst pools) and autoscale policies defined and linked to ticketed ENG work
Dashboards with canary metrics (latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost delta) created and validated
milestones: 2026-03-22: Cohort segmentation and priority mapping complete
2026-04-05: Canary window schedule and test plan published
2026-05-30: First retirement tranche executed for v1 models
decisions: Adopt three-phase cohort rollout (pilot -> ramp -> general) to reduce blast radius
Retire v1 small and med variants first to preserve SLA for enterprise cohorts
Use runtime-1.22 telemetry tags to separate traffic and enable cost comparison
Default rollback threshold: 5% aggregate error rate increase OR p95 latency +30% over baseline
open_questions: Should enterprise customers get a separate migration runway or negotiate custom retention?
Do we provide an optional opt-in flag for customers to test new model variants before cohort promotion?
What is cross-team SLA for fixing canary-detected regressions (SRE 24h/ENG 72h)?
Are there regulatory constraints for retiring models used in customer workflows in EU region?
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Initial RFC posted and reviewed by Product Leadership; feedback requested on cohort definitions
2026-02-28: SRE provided early capacity estimates; recommended a 15% burst pool for pilot phase
2026-03-04: UX provided comms templates and in-console banners for impacted customers
2026-03-11: ENG-23100 capacity hedge PR opened; initial smoke tests passed in staging
risks_mitigation: Risk: Unexpected quality regression when switching model variants -> Mitigation: staggered canaries and automated scoring against baseline prompts
Risk: Customer confusion and support surge -> Mitigation: in-console opt-out, targeted emails, and a dedicated escalation channel
Risk: Insufficient capacity during ramp -> Mitigation: pre-provision burst GPUs and holdback 10% of allocation for emergency fallback
Risk: Rollback automation false positives -> Mitigation: include human-in-the-loop approval for enterprise cohort rollbacks
rollout_plan: Pilot (2 weeks) - internal + 3 external beta customers: monitor 20 baseline prompts and cost delta
Ramp (4 weeks) - cohorts: free -> starter -> selected enterprise; expand telemetry and surface per-customer deltas
General availability - open to all customers with migration docs and in-console migration tool
Retirement tranche - retire v1.small and v1.medium after 30 days of stable GA metrics
metrics: Adoption: % customers migrated per cohort per week
Quality: evaluation set pass rate and human review feedback for 200 critical prompts
Reliability: p50/p95 latency and 99th percentile error rate during canary windows
Economics: per-token cost delta and net change in unit cost after batching/quantization tweaks
Support: number of tickets and median time-to-resolution during rollout
